subject: Third‑party artifact custody matrix and escalation path for PentestCo transfer
messages:
From: Natalie Ruiz <natalie.ruiz@pentestco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transfer of pentest artifacts + custody questions

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for scheduling the on‑site testing window next week. Before we start the final validation pass, legal asked me to confirm the mechanics for transferring raw artefacts and partial findings back to PentestCo and for your team to store copies for remediation validation. A couple quick questions so we can scope the deliverable and timing: 

- What transfer mechanisms do you prefer for large captures (pcap / vm snapshots)? SFTP, encrypted share, or a temporary object store?
- What is Redwood's retention/custody policy for third‑party test artefacts? (how long do you keep copies, who can access them)
- Any SLA for escalations if artefacts indicate active ransomware or critical data exfil?

We typically package artifacts in an encrypted tarball and provide a transfer manifest. If you have a custody matrix or an intake flow we can align with, please send it — otherwise we can follow your preferred process.

Attaching our standard transfer guidance.

Attachments: pentest-transfer-guidelines.pdf

Cheers,
Natalie Ruiz
Engagement Lead — PentestCo Ltd.
mobile: +1 (415) 555-0188

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Ruiz <natalie.ruiz@pentestco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transfer of pentest artifacts + custody questions

Hi Natalie —

Appreciate the note. I've put together a short custody matrix and the minimal SLA triggers so we can close this pre‑engagement housekeeping. High level answers first: SFTP (with key exchange) or an encrypted object store (pre‑signed URL) are both fine; for very large VM snapshots we prefer an object store link. We keep third‑party artefacts for 90 days by default and limit access to the security and engineering triage groups; Legal exceptions can extend/shorten retention. For critical incidents (ransomware, confirmed exfil with active indicators) we have a 2‑hour on‑call escalation target.

See the attached custody matrix (custody-matrix-v1.xlsx) — it maps transfer channel, storage class, retention, and escalation owner. Can you confirm PentestCo's preferred transfer method and whether you will publish the manifest with SHA256 checksums? Also, do you require a PO or a signed SLA addendum before transfer?

If you prefer a quick call to finalize, I can slot 15 minutes today at 4pm PT.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

Attachments: custody-matrix-v1.xlsx

From: Chris O'Neill <chris.oneill@pentestco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Natalie Ruiz <natalie.ruiz@pentestco.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 14:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transfer of pentest artifacts + custody questions

Jordan — thanks for the fast turnaround. We can do SFTP with keypairs and will include a manifest + SHA256. For the VM snapshots we'll push to a pre‑signed object store link (AWS S3) and will mark objects as encrypted at rest. We generally expect vendor retention to match your retention policy; 90 days is acceptable.

Regarding a PO/SLA: our standard approach is a quick signature of a transfer addendum (2 paragraphs + a short escalation matrix) rather than a PO for one‑off engagements. If you can share the addendum text I can route to our procurement team. Otherwise a DocuSign envelope works for us.

I'm attaching the SFTP host fingerprint and a short checklist so your ops team can verify uploads.

Attachments: pentest-sftp-credentials.txt, pentest-transfer-checklist.md

Looping in Neha on the legal/contract side. Natalie/Chris — thanks for confirming the transfer method. Two items from infra/legal that we need to close before you upload: 

1) A short SLA addendum that includes our 2‑hour escalation target for active incidents, a 90‑day retention clause, and an explicit statement that PentestCo will provide SHA256 manifests for each archive. We can draft a one‑page addendum.
2) Confirmation whether PentestCo will upload artifacts to the SFTP host or whether you prefer that Redwood pulls from a pre‑signed S3 URL. If you do the push to our SFTP, provide key fingerprint and user name (we've received the credentials sample already).

If both are ✓ we can open the intake bucket and hand off operations. If you prefer, I can circulate the addendum draft.

—Marcus

Subject: Re: Transfer of pentest artifacts + custody questions

Thanks all — I reviewed Marcus's summary and drafted the two short clauses below that will serve as the transfer addendum. I can put this into DocuSign if PentestCo confirms acceptance.

--- draft clauses ---
1) Transfer & Retention: PentestCo will transfer cryptographically signed artefact archives (manifested with SHA256) to Redwood Inference via mutually agreed secure transport (SFTP with key‑exchange or pre‑signed object store links). Redwood will store transferred artefacts in encrypted object storage for a standard period of 90 days from receipt unless otherwise directed by a mutually signed amendment.

2) Incident Escalation: If transferred artefacts indicate an active, exploitable critical vulnerability or confirmed data exfiltration, Redwood Inference will notify PentestCo and initiate on‑call incident procedures with a target acknowledgment window of 2 hours and a remediation coordination window of 24 hours.

If that language looks good to PentestCo we will: (A) generate a 1‑page addendum, (B) send via DocuSign to the PentestCo procurement contact, and (C) open the intake bucket for the scheduled upload.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachments: requested-contract-clause-snippet.docx
